text: Can, could, may, might, will, would, shall, should and must do not describe an action; they comment on it: how possible, how necessary, how polite. And they obey five rules. One: no s in the third person: he can swim, not he cans. Two: a bare infinitive, without to: she must go. Only ought keeps to. Three: no do in questions or negatives: can he drive? Four: never two modals together: not will can, but will be able to. Five: no ing form and no participle; for those, use a semi modal like be able to.
